memories.content: Mark unverified schedule assumptions as such.
Mark unverified recruitment assumptions as such.
Mark unverified technical assumptions as such.
Clarify which stage of prototype fabrication or user study each requested resource is used for.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the personnel assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the equipment assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the time allocated to each procedure.
Verify that the planned number of formative evaluation iterations is feasible within the time for prototype modification and recruitment resources.
Include only the minimum functionality required to compare primary design assumptions in the scope of the formative evaluation prototype.
The user's iterative design plan can be judged feasible only if time and personnel are allocated for modifying the prototype between iterations.
Delays in participant recruitment can compress the time available for prototype modification between formative evaluations.
Do not change names referring to the same user roles, system functions, or operational stages midway.
Use abbreviations only for long recurring terms in a two-page proposal.
Present the full term and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Refer to participants based on the roles they perform in the study rather than their status.
Reviewers from different subfields find it difficult to infer an abbreviation from context alone when it is not defined at first use.
When introducing an operational role for the first time, define both the decisions it can make and the actions it performs.
Individuals holding identical job titles may possess different system modification privileges and data access rights depending on their deployment site.
The user tends to group distinct field roles under the single label “user.”

analysis.overview: The frames address complementary concerns without semantic overlap or disagreement. The reference frame focuses on feasibility, resource staging, prototype scope, and uncertainty disclosure; the compared frame focuses on terminology, abbreviations, and precise role definitions.

relations.reason: These memories split one disclosure policy across three assumption domains, with no corresponding claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Unverified schedule, recruitment, and technical assumptions should be explicitly identified as unverified.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers stable terminology, restrained and defined abbreviations, role-based participant naming, explicit operational authority, and site-dependent privileges.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame covers disclosure of unverified assumptions, procedure-level feasibility, resource staging, prototype scope, and iteration risks involving modification and recruitment.
